title: Savings account, zero-balance accounts and interest tax
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: A savings account keeps money safe and accessible and pays modest interest — typically around 2.5–4% at large banks and somewhat more at some small-finance banks and digital banks. Interest is added to your taxable income; under the old regime you can deduct up to ₹10,000 of savings-account interest under Section 80TTA. Many banks require a minimum average balance and charge a penalty if you fall below it; a zero-balance (basic savings) account avoids this. Deposits are insured by DICGC up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank. Use one account for salary and bills, a second for savings so you do not spend it, and keep your mobile number and email updated with the bank for alerts. Avoid parking large idle balances here when a sweep-in FD or liquid fund would earn more.
summary_hinglish: Savings account mein byaj lagbhag 2.5-4% (kuch small finance banks mein zyada). Old regime mein ₹10,000 tak byaj par 80TTA ki chhoot. Minimum balance na ho to penalty lag sakti hai, zero-balance account se bacha ja sakta hai. DICGC har bank mein ₹5 lakh tak insure karta hai. Bachat ke liye alag account rakho.
summary_hi: बचत खाते पर लगभग 2.5-4% ब्याज मिलता है। पुराने रिजीम में ₹10,000 तक के ब्याज पर 80TTA की छूट है। मिनिमम बैलेंस न रखने पर जुर्माना लग सकता है, ज़ीरो-बैलेंस खाता इससे बचाता है। DICGC हर बैंक में ₹5 लाख तक सुरक्षित करता है। बचत के लिए अलग खाता रखें।
